tool.name: greynoise_classify
tool.description:
Classify an IPv4 address as targeted-attacker / opportunistic-noise / benign-known via GreyNoise. Second 🔴 critical item from the §10 expert-pentester gap audit. Highest-leverage IR-triage signal: distinguishes opportunistic-internet-noise IPs (mass scanners like Shodan/Censys) from targeted attackers.
GreyNoise's core insight is the `noise` flag:
| Signal | Meaning | |---|---| | `noise: true, classification: benign` | Known-benign mass scanner (Shodan, Censys, search-engine bots) | | `noise: true, classification: malicious` | Mass scanner that's also been observed performing malicious activity | | `noise: true, classification: unknown` | Mass scanner — not yet classified | | `noise: false, classification: malicious` | **Targeted attacker** (this IP isn't mass-scanning everyone, it's specifically interacting with you) | | `noise: false, classification: benign` | Targeted-but-benign (legitimate enterprise scanner) | | no record | GreyNoise has no observation of this IP |
Plus the **RIOT** ("Rule It Out") signal: when an IP is on a known-benign list (Apple iCloud relay, Cloudflare, Akamai edge, Microsoft 365), the response carries `riot: true` with `name`/`category` describing what the IP belongs to. RIOT lets the agent suppress alerts for demonstrably benign infrastructure.
Severity tuning: - **High** (CWE-453, malicious_target) — `noise: false, classification: malicious` (**targeted attacker**). - **Medium** (CWE-453) — `noise: true, classification: malicious` (opportunistic but flagged-malicious mass scanner). - *(no finding)* — `noise: true, classification: benign` (Shodan etc.), RIOT-listed benign IPs, or no observation. Treated as background internet noise that shouldn't generate triage work.
Auth: - Community v3 API works **without a key** (anonymous tier). - `STRIX_GREYNOISE_KEY` (paid tier) raises rate limit + adds richer per-IP context. - RIOT v2 API **requires the paid key** — silently skipped without it (recorded as `riot.skipped=True`).
Cache: per-IP JSON cache under `~/.strix/greynoise_cache/`, 6-hour TTL. Stale-cache served when both Community + RIOT fail (fail-open with `error` populated). Cache hit re-emits findings from cached data. Disable with `STRIX_GREYNOISE_NO_CACHE=1`.
Each finding carries severity-tailored `description_plain` + `recommended_action` (high → investigate as targeted attack, correlate with logs, block at perimeter, cross-reference VT; medium → lower-priority block at WAF/firewall, add to denylist). `verification_status=needs_review` since classifications shift as GreyNoise observes more activity.
MITRE technique: T1596 (Search Open Technical Databases).
Composes with cluster-A safety: rate-limit applies; `--exclude-path` doesn't apply (URLs are api.greynoise.io, not the customer's domain).

parameter.name: ip
parameter.description: IPv4 address (private/loopback/link-local rejected; IPv6 not supported by the GreyNoise free tier). Examples: `1.1.1.1`, `8.8.8.8`, `203.0.113.5` (would be rejected as it's a documentation range — Python's ipaddress flags it as private).

returns.description:
{success, ip, queried_at, from_cache, community: {present, noise, classification, name, link, last_seen, riot, code, message, error?}, riot: {present, name, category, trust_level, description, last_updated, error?, skipped?, reason?}, severity, findings_emitted, error?}.
The agent should: 1. **Suppress findings** for IPs flagged as `community.noise=True, classification=benign` or `riot.present=True` — those are confirmed benign infrastructure. 2. **Escalate** on `severity=high` (targeted-malicious) — these represent real-time attack surface. 3. Cross-reference high-severity GreyNoise verdicts with `vt_reputation` (#71) for additional vendor consensus.
